main_text.l: 1.Pet.2.ver.24.) seu pœnas sufficientes, tempore quidem finitas, valore tamen & vigore, tum propter dignitatem seu prœstantiam PERSONÆ (Actor. 20. 28. Rom. 8.3. 1.Joh. 1.7.) tum ob gravitatem cruciatuum, (Psal. 22. Jes. 53. v. 5. 10. 11. Matth. 26. & 27. Actor. 2.24. Heb. 5..7.) & ignominiæ (Jes. 53.12. Matth. 26. &c.) infinitas, pœnisq; æternis æquivalen-tes pro nobis persolvit, atque ita nobis Justitiam & Remissionem peccatorū, viramq; æternam ꝓmeruit. (Dan. 9. 24. 26. Rom. 3.24. & 4.6. Gal. 3.4. 5. Heb. 10.19.)

CHRISTUS ergo per supplicium crucis sentiens in illo iram Dei (Matth. 27.46.) adversus peccata, ꝑsolvit pœnas illis debitas, (Rom. 3.24.25. Eph. 1.7.) seu satisfecit ꝓ peccatis nostris, Col. 2.13.14, seu deniq; illa expiavit, (1.Joh. 2.1. Jes. 53.10. 2.Cor. 5.21, Rom. 3.25.) nosq; à ma-ledictione legis, & ab omni potestate Diaboli redemit. (Gal. 3.13. Heb. 9.12. Rō. 1.14.) Atq; hinc patet, cur Christus tā-topere ab illo supplicio abhorruerit, tamque ardenti querulatione illud de-preçatus sit, (Matth. 26.38.) cum tamen Marty-

page.notes: Uncertain readings: "ꝑsolvit" (the abbreviated word after "peccata," is hard to make out, so it is read as persolvit); "Rō." in the last scripture reference; "26.38" in the final reference. "CHRISTUS" is set as a small-capital opening word. The superscript "ꝓ" marks in "ꝓmeruit" and "ꝓ peccatis" are read as pro. The page ends mid-word with "Marty-", continued on the next page.
